accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 45, printed 31, lines 2-3: document-level constraint identification, subdivided into spelling and uniqueness.
The C identifier combines a one- or two-digit clause number with a two- or three-digit sequence within that clause. Unlike the R convention, a constraint sequence can have three digits.
The identifier uniquely names the constraint. It is source metadata, not a requirement for a compiler to emit that identifier or a particular severity.
PDF 45 lines 4-6: association notation, incorporation into a syntax term, and propagation to every occurrence are separately accounted.
An associated syntax-rule number appears parenthetically on a constraint. Association is common, not universal.
An associated constraint participates in the definition of its syntax term; the production cannot be interpreted in isolation from it.

The associated constraint follows the term at all its occurrences, not just the displayed production. R403/C401 and its actual IF context are handled in 4.1.3; other terms retain their defining owners. Establishing the complete use graph needs independent source-census review, not duplicate local S IDs.
PDF 45 lines 7-12: distinguishes unassociated constraints, reporting capability, broader textual restrictions, and the narrower diagnostic subset.
A constraint without a parenthesized syntax association still restricts programs, similarly to a restriction written in prose.

PDF 45 lines 7-9 cross-reference the processor's capability to detect and report constraint violations. This real obligation is owned by 4.2 p2(3), with an explicit pending capability contract under S4.2-003; it is not discarded as merely definitional.

PDF 45 lines 9-11: a broad textual requirement and a numbered constraint covering only part of it can coexist. A conforming program must satisfy the full textual requirement, not only the numbered subset.

PDF 45 lines 10-12: numbering the subset does not require diagnostic capability for every violation of the broader prose. Separate 4.2 obligations, including source-form, characters, unsupported kinds, and scope rules, must still be checked. Capability is not mandatory fatal rejection on each invocation. The 4.2 p3 FORMAT exception also remains applicable.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and tested integration repairs: doc/source_audits/batch_006.json. Constraint conventions and their distinction from broader textual restrictions are preserved. Explanatory conventions do not themselves require an arbitrary diagnostic program.
